motion.name: dur-sheet-out
motion.purpose: Mobile sheet closing.

motion.purpose: Legendary foil sweep.

motion.name: chibi-frame
motion.purpose: Each drawn chibi frame, never tweened.

motion.name: press-depth / raise / rise
motion.purpose: Distances, all zero under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: track-draw
motion.value: scaleY(0) to scaleY(1) from the top, 160ms, var(--ease-in-out), delay stop * 160ms + 120ms
motion.purpose: Each career track segment draws down to the next stop on arrival.

motion.name: stop-pop
motion.value: opacity 0, scale(0.5) to 1, 320ms, var(--ease-pop), delay stop * 160ms
motion.purpose: Each career stop disc pops onto the track on arrival, 160ms after the one above.

motion.name: medal-turn
motion.purpose: A medal turns to its back on slot hover (fine pointers) or press; faces swap without turning under reduced motion.

motion.name: replay-hover
motion.value: thumbnail scale(1.03) over 300ms; play disc opacity 0 and translateY(8px) to rest over var(--dur-hover); both var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A replay tile's thumbnail zooms and its play disc rises on hover; the disc is always visible on touch.

motion.name: unlock-arrival
motion.purpose: The foil crosses the unlock banner once on arrival; hidden under reduced motion.

motion.name: showcase-pace
motion.purpose: Coin physics, spin, shimmer and the cheque's bob are scaled per 60fps frame and capped, so the showcase runs at the same pace at any frame rate. Paused (and on arrival under reduced motion) everything holds and the canvas renders on demand; orbiting still works.

cues.tick: B5, very quiet, hover, fine pointers only, max one per 60ms
cues.press: A4, secondary controls without their own cue
cues.tab: D4 E4 F#4 A4 B4 D5 in menu order
cues.confirm: D4+A4 then D5, the Play button
cues.toggleOn: A4 to D5 (also choosing a mode or a palette), also playing the showcase
cues.toggleOff: D5 to A4, also pausing the showcase
cues.unlock: D4 F#4 A4 D5 then coin.mp3, legendary achievement
cues.boop: random D5-B5 with a 2-semitone bend, banner chibi
cues.miss: A3 to F#3, errors (defined, not yet wired)
cues.throw: coin.mp3, throwing a coin in the MDF 2025 showcase (click, tap or the throw button)
cues.clink: impact.mp3 then a quiet random D5-B5, a thrown coin landing on the cheque; at most once per coin every 500ms; ambient coins are silent

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Player Profile"**

The site is Lucas's player profile in a cosy game client. The sidebar is the client chrome: the player card with the chibi head in its live status ring, the tabs (the lowercase menu), the friends panel where his Discord presence lives, the settings row (sound, Locale, theme) and the socials. The content panel is the profile screen: on the home page a banner with who he is and the team he plays for right now, a showcase of real achievements with MasterDevFrance 2025 as the legendary one, an inventory of featured Projects framed by rarity, an about slot beside his hobbies, the FAQ, and a goodbye. Every stat on screen is a real fact from `content/` or a live source; the game is the frame, never the claim.

It is a cosy client, not a competitive one: a deep navy night (or, in the second palette, deep plum), soft fat corners, chunky buttons that sink onto a ledge when pressed, warm off-white text, candy rarity colours, and a single action colour that means "this is the thing to press": off-white standing on an electric-blue ledge at night, electric blue by day, tangerine in the plum palette. Pressable things answer with one note of a single instrument, so moving around the site plays a little melody, and one visible switch silences it all.

Density is relaxed: big slots with generous gaps, one focal object per row. The voice stays as PRODUCT.md binds it (first person, "Yoooo", emojis, lowercase menu labels). Anti-references: the previous "Dev's Desk" zinc shell (colour only through content, no accent), terminal or IDE costumes, near-black with a glowing neon accent (electric blue is a solid ledge and an underline here, never a glow), hextech gold trim (gold belongs to the legendary rarity alone), and esports HUD aggression (angular chamfers, scanlines, rank emblems).
keyCharacteristics: Two-zone client inside a 12px frame: a 320px sidebar beside a rounded profile panel, both on the palette's ground, the panel the only part that scrolls.

Two palettes, each with a dark and a light mode, all through the same role tokens: "electric" (the default; navy night in dark, off-white daytime in light) and "plum" (the plum and tangerine client). Dark is the default mode.
One action colour for the Play button, the active tab, the sound switch when on and selection; its ink colour draws focus.
Rarity colours (common, rare, epic, legendary) frame content by its rarity field, never decoration.
Chunky pressable controls on a solid ledge; raised slots and cards with soft 16px corners and a moulded-tray highlight.
A one-instrument kalimba kit in D major pentatonic, on by default, behind an always-visible switch.
The chibi is the mascot: stepped-frame poses on the banner, in the hobbies, the presence card and the goodbye.

The other profile screens open on a page banner and keep the game's objects: the career path of stops on a track, diplomas as medals that turn like coins, the loadout's bags of Techs in sunken wells, and replay tiles; the legendary achievement's own page is the reward screen of its unlock: an unlock banner, then the cheque on its stage in a showcase where the visitor throws coins.

rules.name: The Palette Owns the Shell Rule
rules.body: The frame, sidebar and panel are the palette's own frame, ground and raised colours (Navy Frame, Navy and Navy Raised in electric dark; Night, Plum and Velvet in plum dark), always through the role tokens. Never fall back to a neutral grey surface with colourful accents; the colour is the room, not the furniture.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: An action fill marks the single most important action or state in its zone: the Play button in the panel, the active tab and the sound switch in the chrome, plus selection; the action ink draws focus. A second action-filled button in the panel means one of them is wrong. In the Admin a save button takes the action fill only while its form holds unpublished changes, so a lit button always has something to publish. A component never names Tangerine, Electric or Off-white directly for this role; it uses `action`, `action-ledge`, `action-ink` and `on-action`, so both palettes follow. Secondary links use the action ink as their text in light; in electric dark they stay ink with an Electric underline and take the action ink on hover.

rules.name: The Rarity Is Data Rule
rules.body: A rarity colour appears only on an item whose rarity field says so, as its 2px frame, 4px top band and tag (and the filled sparkle on legendary). Never use the rarity hues for headings, backgrounds or decoration. Inside the legendary item's own showcase the scene is the item, so the cheque's stage rim (its top band in 3D) and the coins are Legendary, the rim Legendary Deep by day.

rules.name: The Computed Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on a colour that is not part of the palette (a Tech's own colour) is whichever of Night or Cream contrasts more, computed; if neither reaches 4.5:1, the chip is drawn as a 2px outline in that colour with the theme's ink instead of a fill.

rules.name: The Copy Keeps Its Case Rule
rules.body: Type is set in the case the copy is written in. Unbounded is never forced to uppercase; the lowercase menu labels and casual voice are binding. The one uppercase string is the two-letter Locale code, in Data.

rules.name: The Typography Primitives Rule
rules.body: Text goes through `components/typography` (Display, Headline, Title, Data, Tag, P, Muted), with the element chosen by `as` so the look never dictates the outline. A raw heading with its own sizes is drift.

rules.name: The Real Button Rule
rules.body: Anything pressable has a ledge and sinks onto it when pressed; anything with a ledge is pressable. Static cards and slots never get one. Ghost and link controls are not raised controls and have none.

rules.name: The Float Means On Top Rule
rules.body: Blurred shadows belong only to layers above the client (the mobile sheet, menus, the Admin's pinned published notice).

dos: **Do** let the palette's own frame, ground and raised colours own the whole shell (Navy Frame #05081c, Navy #0a0f2e and Navy Raised #141c48 by default), through the role tokens rather than fixed colours, so every component works in both palettes and both modes.

**Do** keep the action fill to the Play button, the active tab, the sound switch when on, selection and, in the Admin, a save button whose form has changes, and the action ink to focus, the menu check and link text.
**Do** derive every stat from `content/`, the dictionaries or a live source (Lanyard, GitHub, YouTube), and hide a missing number rather than show zero.
**Do** compute the ink on Tech colours and use the deep `-ink` variants for coloured text in light.
**Do** give every pressable control a ledge, a 44px target and a note from the kit (the Admin's controls stay silent).
**Do** use an outline button (ground fill, 2px seam border) for secondary actions sitting on a raised surface.
**Do** keep the sound switch visible on every page that plays sound (the Admin plays none) and honour reduced motion for both motion and sound.
**Do** write every new string in both Locales and keep the lowercase, casual voice.
donts: **Don't** invent game stats: no level, rank, XP, KDA, win rate or achievement Lucas did not earn.
**Don't** use rarity colours for decoration, headings or backgrounds.
**Don't** hard-code Tangerine, Electric, Off-white or Night for the action or for text on a bright fill; use `action`, `action-ledge`, `action-ink`, `on-action` and `on-bright`.
**Don't** drift into esports HUD aggression: no chamfered corners, scanlines, hex grids, glowing neon edges or forced uppercase.
**Don't** go back to neutral zinc surfaces with colour only from content.
**Don't** play sound automatically, on hover for touch pointers, from presence updates, or anywhere the visitor cannot silence it.
**Don't** put blur or soft shadows on anything that does not float above the client.
**Don't** let the chibi hop, slide or tween; its movement lives in its drawn frames.
**Don't** make the presence card disappear or change height; it always shows a state.
